name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.177.0 — The replay tree is the reviewed tree: each review now records the two commits bounding what it judged as refs under refs/spec-review/<runId>/ — judged at the close row's head sha, close at the close commit — written best-effort so a failed write can never block a close. The replay harness reads that pair instead of asking which commit last touched the spec file, refuses (exit 4) a row that cannot name its own bounds, and reconstructs the pre-ref backlog only through the new run-once replay.js --backfill-pins. Setup re-derives the target's own AC coverage against the tree it assembled and exits 5 with a diagnosis rather than printing a success line over a tree the review never saw. 7.176.0 — The review page paints every marked area on its screen previews at all times — a numbered orange pin on the box, the same id on its note row — and the whole row is the click target, so selecting a note lights its box and clicking a box highlights its note. A box belongs to the state it was drawn on, and selecting its note switches the screen to that state. Each board gains an eye toggle that hides its marks, the composer gains a Mark an area action, and a mark now reads as a highlighter tint inside a dashed frame held clear of the content so it can never be mistaken for a border. Addressing a region note re-anchors its box against the edited mock in headless Chrome before the note turns amber, reporting a lost box rather than guessing; the client mount stores and re-places regions, drawing works by long-press on touch, and the atlas index cards carry per-screen open and needs-you counts. 7.175.0 — A wireframe now carries no styles of its own: it links only the three named stylesheet layers — the shared register, the shared kit, and the project's own kit — and a project's own vocabulary lives in that one file, which may not redefine or outgrow the shared kit it extends. Every design-atlas.js check run over a resolved project kit now prints its size against the shared kit's own, its rules used on exactly one screen, and its layout share — the proportion of its rules that are pure layout rather than styling, the number a deferred component-kit decision reads.
